premises.text: Girls' toys are low-tech and unfair versus boys' high-tech toys, while girls care about friendship and communication and deserve better tech
premises.evidence_span: Girls are just as smart and they deserve a lot better

premises.text: JewelBots are wearables with patent-pending device-to-device mesh networking so girls can use and program them without a phone
premises.evidence_span: Jewelbots is the first wearable device to communicate from device to device

premises.text: Friendship color groups, proximity glow, and customizable light/vibration secret messages enable phone-free social signaling
premises.evidence_span: Jewelbots can be used to send messages, so girls can send each other secret messages in their own languages

premises.text: JewelBots are open-source Arduino-programmable via micro USB for custom effects and interactions
premises.evidence_span: Jewelbots are completely open source. So girls can code them to do whatever they imagine

premises.text: COPPA-compliant communication plus interchangeable charms/bands sold separately for collect-and-trade
premises.evidence_span: Jewelbots are also COPPA compliant, so the girls can communicate with each other completely safely

premises.text: Sold online in packs ($69–$139) with Cartoon Network Powerpuff Girls and Google Made with Code licensing partnerships
premises.evidence_span: JewelBots are sold online for $69 for one, $99 for the two-pack, and $139 for the Bestie three-pack

value.text: Girls get a high-tech wearable that makes friendship, secret messaging, and coding feel empowering and fun
value.evidence_span: every girl feels empowered to become an engineer
